text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- Higher living standards, decreased unemployment and inflation as well as continued economic growth were the most important economic developments this year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's food prices rose by 0.3 percent between December 10 and 20 compared with the previous 10 days and by 2.3 percent compared with the same period in November.

- Up to five plants will be privatised by the year-end. They are the Krasnystaw-based Cersanit sanitary ceramics maker, the Lezajsk brewery, the Emit engine maker in Zychlin and two meat processing plants in Elk and Tarnow, the treasury ministry state secretary for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.

- Shares of Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist, will be offered on the Warsaw bourse and international stock exchanges at the start of 1998. The process of TPSA's privatisation will start next year, the telecommunications minister Andrzej Zielinski said.

- The authorities of the city of Lodz, central Poland, have decided to create a special economic zone in the province which should give an additional 6,500 jobs and boost the region's economic development, the municipal authorities said.

- The Netia Telekom Ostrowiec SA regional telecom firm has received first prize for its support for local self-government initiatives in the Malopolska region, southern Poland, awarded by the Nowy Sacz-based Higher School of Business.

- As of 1997, Polish zloty notes will be printed in Poland and not in Britain, although the cost will be 57 percent higher than the previous price, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz Waltz said.

- Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI)-10 made a net loss of 6.2 million zlotys in the first three quarters of 1996. Of the 34 companies controlled by fund, 18 made profits and 14 losses, the Fund said.
- The state treasury sold only 77 percent of the Kruszwica oil and fat maker shares' offered yesterday. Over 1.25 million shares were sold at 25 zlotys a share, the treasury said.
- The Lomza-based Pepees meat producer has presented the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) with its share issue prospectus.
- Poland's Business Centre Club (BCC), the biggest employers' lobby, has awarded former privatisation ministers Janusz Lewandowski and Wieslaw Kaczmarek the BCC's Golden Statue awards.
